digest.component_or_area: GitHub Actions CI workflow and pytest infrastructure
propositions: macOS pytest temporary Git repositories are created on runner.temp, which may suffer filesystem latency during high-volume small-write workloads like git-add/git-commit pairs in the N=3000 import benchmark

a hypothesis to reduce critical-path time on macOS was to provision an ephemeral APFS RAM disk and route pytest basetemp writes there instead of runner.temp, following precedent from Apple Git CI and Aeron

four independent treatment measurements (runs 31869753711, 31869919362, 31870391571, 31873067707) each showed slower default-suite wall times (18m26s–20m54s) than the exact no-RAM control (17m26s), failing to meet the predeclared 5% or larger-observed-range retention threshold

the RAM-disk experiment also exposed a defect in recursive basetemp cleanup: intentionally owner-nonwritable workflow snapshot fixtures raised PermissionError during recursive removal, fixed by restoring owner write permission before rm -rf

the experiment was rejected per AC7 and fully reverted; the RAM-disk lifecycle, reporting, and contract tests were removed and both pytest tiers restored to runner.temp with unchanged selectors, markers, xdist workers, timeouts, and collection counts

nested pytest in the cleanup oracle inherited cacheprovider from the outer process, creating an unexpected .pytest_cache artifact that leaked into collection; the defect was fixed by passing -p no:cacheprovider to the nested subprocess
